about: What the story-world generators can build and perform. fyt/worldgen.py builds its schemas, guides and guards from this file and renderer/src/scenes/world/storyworld/ draws from it, so a verb, set kind or style added here (and drawn there) is open to every later video. Nothing here is a finished asset: every character, creature, object and place is generated from a per-video design.

styles.lowpoly: stylised low-poly 3D, flat-shaded facets, soft daylight, gentle fog: the default for stories of people, animals and places
styles.voxel: blocky voxel world (box people and box creatures, nearest-neighbour textures), bright toy-like colours: playful simulations and what-if stories
styles.noir: dark atmospheric incident explainer: night or overcast, cold fog, rim light, glowing overlays: accidents, emergencies, crimes, mysteries
styles.diorama: documentary miniature: a warm tilted-shift tabletop of the place, paper-like materials, soft shadows: history and investigations
styles.clinical: clean scientific visualisation: white or deep-blue void, glossy translucent materials, cool rim light: medicine, biology, physics

humanoid.describe: a person (by role and clothing, never a real person's likeness)

bird.describe: a bird or other winged creature

fish.describe: a fish, whale, shark or other swimmer

insect.describe: an insect, spider or other many-legged small creature

vehicle.describe: a car, truck, aircraft, helicopter, boat, train or bicycle

object.describe: a thing people use or carry: a bag, a tool, a phone, a package, a bottle, a device

structure.describe: a building, tower, bridge, tent or other built place

plant.describe: a tree, flower, crop or fungus

cell.describe: a cell, virus, bacterium, organ or other body part, shown as a model

sets.forest: woodland: trees of the story's kind, undergrowth, a trail
sets.grassland: open meadow or prairie, scattered bushes and rocks
sets.desert: sand or scrub, dunes or mesas, cacti or dry brush
sets.beach: sand meeting the sea, palms or dunes
sets.river: a river running through land, banks and reeds
sets.town: a small street of low buildings
sets.road: a road through open land, poles and signs
sets.airfield: a runway, a hangar and a windsock
sets.room: an interior: walls, floor, a window, furniture
sets.hall: a large interior: columns, high ceiling
sets.hospital: a clinic or operating room: bed, lamps, monitors
sets.cave: rock walls and a dim opening
sets.underwater: below the surface: seabed, light shafts, particles
sets.sky: among clouds, the ground far below
sets.micro: inside a body or a sample: fluid, drifting particles, soft walls

camera.establish: high and wide, slowly descending onto the place and who is in it
camera.follow: tracking alongside the main actor as it moves
camera.push_in: slowly moving in to a close shot of the main actor
camera.low_angle: low, looking up at the main actor, making it loom
camera.over_shoulder: behind one actor, looking at another
camera.top_down: looking straight down on the scene, like a map
camera.reveal: rising from close behind something to show the whole scene

marks.beam: a glowing line from one actor to another (a signal, a call, a line of sight)
marks.arrow: an arrow showing where one actor goes or what it points at
marks.path: a dotted path on the ground along the main actor's route
marks.ring: a pulsing ring on the ground around an actor (here, this one)
marks.dome: a wireframe dome over an actor (a range, a reach, coverage)
marks.glow: the actor glows to draw the eye
